stem.text: A function f has derivative \( f'(x) = \frac{2\left(x + 4\right)\left(x - 2\right)}{x} \) for all \( x \ne 0 \), where f is not defined at \( x = 0 \). On what open intervals is f decreasing? Give a reason for the answer.

answer_key.label: f is decreasing on the intervals \( (-\infty, -4) \) and \( (0, 2) \), because \( f'(x) < 0 \) on each of those intervals.

worked_solution.text: The sign of f' can change only where \( f'(x) = 0 \) at \( x = -4 \) and \( x = 2 \), and f' is undefined at \( x = 0 \), which is not in the domain of f.
worked_solution.rule_named: partition points of the sign chart

worked_solution.text: Testing one point in each piece gives \( f'(x) < 0 \) on the intervals \( (-\infty, -4) \) and \( (0, 2) \) and \( f'(x) > 0 \) on the intervals \( (-4, 0) \) and \( (2, \infty) \).
So f is decreasing on the intervals \( (-\infty, -4) \) and \( (0, 2) \), because \( f'(x) < 0 \) on each of those intervals.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign of the derivative gives the direction of the function
